question: Does online anchor-domain loss change improve expert-group update decisions beyond a specified strong progress baseline?
scope: Protect a designated pretrained anchor domain A while adapting to B. Scalar control of a fixed expert parameter group; not expert coordination or full-history continual retention.

model.selection: Fixed a priori indices; no outcome-based expert selection. Record token exposure, displacement and downstream routing changes.
model.frozen: all parameters other than the named experts, including routers, attention, norms, embeddings and output head

development.label_objective: Report the two-dimensional (B selection improvement, A selection deterioration) outcome. No fabricated optimal-action labels until feasibility/objective is calibrated and locked.

data.format: JSONL documents with id, source, domain A/B, text; source identifies a document family, not an entire corpus
data.split: Global source-group hash split before tokenization, fixed across roots: train/monitor/selection/test=70/10/10/10. Deduplicate normalized full documents before splitting; reject cross-domain duplicates.
data.test_access: Preflight/development runner never tokenizes or evaluates test documents. Splitting may hash identifiers/text for integrity.
data.leakage_limits: Exact dedup does not prove no near-duplicates or no overlap with model pretraining. Final corpus review is required before confirmatory lock.
data.candidate_A: WikiText encyclopedia articles reconstructed from paragraph rows
data.candidate_B: CPython standard-library source files grouped by package, pinned version; code adaptation rather than general coding benchmark
data.selection_limits: Repeated development-selection queries are development evidence only. Roots sharing documents are not domain-generalization samples.

branching.restore: All mutable parameters, FP32 master parameters, optimizer moments/steps, Python/numpy/torch/CUDA RNG, data stream state and training flag; frozen model shared immutably and checked
branching.future_pairing: Within a checkpoint/future all actions see identical B batches; future 1 is an independent resampling continuation, not another root
branching.evaluation: Pure token-weighted shifted language-model CE, excluding padding and auxiliary router loss
branching.costs: Count actual prefix, branches, train tokens, evaluated tokens, restoration time, wall time and peak GPU memory; branches are not free
branching.unit: Independent history/root. Keep all checkpoints and action branches from one root in the same outer split.

later_lock_required: Final corpus revisions, document/source manifests, contamination review and fixed token budgets
Learning-rate/calibration search budget and selected stable adaptation configuration
B monitor target and independent selection/final-test checks; first-hit rule and failure handling
Branch feasibility/objective, minimum meaningful effect, tie handling and ranking-regret definition
Independent training/development/confirmation history allocation and root-level uncertainty analysis
Strong fixed/time/progress baselines, matched query costs, model capacity and hyperparameter search budgets
A single preregistered confirmation analysis; no day-7 significance-based stopping
decision: Hardware/engineering gate first; then stable B held-out learning and measurement resolution. No requirement that forgetting be large or an intermediate multiplier win. An inconclusive pilot does not establish zero information.
smoke: Tiny randomly initialized Hugging Face OLMoE with generated token sequences, CPU only. Engineering verification, never evidence about pretrained language MoE or feedback benefit.
